name: no-time
title: No time to type
kicker: Why this talk · the second ground
html:
No time to type

/remote-control

Most of my work is steered by thumb, from a phone, through Claude Code’s /remote-control. The session runs on my machine; I answer it from wherever I am.

Safe while nobody watches

Offered only what the state allows. A refusal says why.

Cheap when repeated

Think once, then replay with no model.

Short to say

A goal in words, not a manual.

So the agent finds its way from the answers, not from me.
say: The second ground is personal. I don't have typing time. Most of my work is steered by thumb, from a phone, through Claude Code's /remote-control: the session runs on my machine, and I answer it from wherever I am. That changes what an agent has to be. It has to be safe while nobody watches every step: it should only be offered what the state allows, and a refusal should say why. It has to be cheap when it does the same thing again: think once, then replay with no model, which is Hightower's point. And what I give it has to be short: a goal in words, not a manual. So the agent has to find its way from the answers, not from me. Hold on to that; it's why the controls have to be in the answers.

deck:ref.summary: Most of my work is steered by thumb, from a phone, through Claude Code's /remote-control, away from the keyboard. So the agents have to act safely while nobody watches every step, and cheaply when they do the same thing again. Hypermedia gives the first (only what the state allows is offered); kept scripts give the second (zero tokens to replay).

deck:ref.title: ZTA: Zero Token Architecture
deck:ref.summary: Agents that run inference on every call burn tokens and work against zero trust. Infer once, then run the result as reliable, deterministic code. (In my words, from the talk's page and Daniel Cranney's write-up.)
deck:ref.quote:
“You are all having way too much fun burning way too many tokens”

His opening line, as quoted in Daniel Cranney, “Infer Once, Run Everywhere: Zero-Token Architecture”, WeAreDevelopers, 13 October 2026.
